transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Well, Dr. Smith, it's... it's a bit hard to talk about, to be honest. I've been working as a general manager at the plant for a long time now, and I usually keep things running smooth, you know? I'm the guy who handles the problems, the one people come to when things go wrong on the floor. But lately, things haven't been right with me. I've been having these... these thoughts. They just kind of creep up on me, especially at night when it's quiet and I'm just lying there. I start thinking that maybe... maybe my family would just be better off if I wasn't around anymore. If I just went to sleep and didn't wake up. It's heavy, you know? It's a really heavy thing to carry around. I tried to just push through it, keep working, keep managing the guys, but it got to be too much. It actually scared me, having those thoughts so clear like that. It scared me enough that I actually went and told my supervisor about it, which is not something I'd ever normally do. I mean, I don't even have an eighth-grade education, but I've worked my way up, and showing weakness like that... it's just not me. But I had to say something, because it's just been weighing on me so much.
Have you ever had a period, lasting several days or more, where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than normal, even if it happened a long time ago?

Well, you know, it's funny you ask that, because... yeah, actually. Not right now, of course, right now I just feel like I'm dragging a ton of bricks behind me, but... there was a time, maybe a few months back, I think? It's hard to keep track of time when you're working the hours I do. But yeah, there was this stretch where I just... I didn't even feel like myself, but in a good way, if that makes sense? 

I mean, usually, I'm pretty beat by the end of a shift at the plant. You're on your feet, you're dealing with shipments, you're putting out fires—figuratively, mostly, thank God—but during this one week, or maybe it was closer to two, I just... I had this motor running inside me that wouldn't quit. I'd be waking up at, I don't know, three, maybe four in the morning, way before the sun was even thinking about coming up, and I wasn't even tired. I'd just lay there for a second and then boom, I'm up. 

And it wasn't just being awake, it was like... I had to *do* things. I remember sitting at the kitchen table with a notepad, just furiously sketching out these whole new plans for reorganizing the entire west wing of the warehouse. I had it all figured out, how to cut loading time by twenty percent, moving the heavy pallets closer to the bay doors. And then, before I even went into work, I'd go out to my garage. My wife's been on me for years to clean that thing out, and I just tore into it. I'm talking pulling everything out onto the driveway in the pitch black, sorting tools, building new shelves from scrap wood I had lying around. 

I'd jump from the garage to fixing the leaky faucet in the downstairs bathroom, then back to the warehouse plans, and I just... I didn't want to stop. I felt like I could take on the whole world and still have energy left over to paint the house. It was like I didn't even need sleep, just a couple of hours and I was ready to go again at a hundred miles an hour. It felt great at the time, honestly, like I was finally getting ahead of everything, but looking back, my wife said I was exhausting just to watch.

During this current low period, have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds that others don't hear, or having thoughts or beliefs—like feeling you've done something terribly wrong or that you're being punished—that you later realized weren't based in reality?

No, no, I've never heard any voices or anything like that. No sounds that aren't there, no feeling like someone's out to get me or punishing me from the outside, nothing crazy like that. But... as far as feeling like I've done something wrong? Yeah. Yeah, that's... that's a whole other thing. That's just a constant loop in my head right now. 

It's about my daughter, mostly. She moved out a while ago, and we just... we don't really talk much anymore. And lately, sitting here feeling so low, I just can't stop playing it all back. I keep going over and over the day she left, and the months before it, the arguments, the quiet dinners where nobody said a word. I just keep telling myself I must have failed her somehow. You know? Like, a better father, a smarter man, somebody who knew how to talk to his kids, he would have done something different. He would have known what to say to make her stay, or at least make her want to call her old man once in a while. 

I just sit there in my recliner, staring at the TV without even watching it, and I think about every time I worked a double shift instead of going to her school things. I thought I was providing, you know? Doing what a man's supposed to do. But now I just feel this heavy, sickening guilt in my stomach, like I ruined everything. Like I'm just fundamentally flawed as a parent. And it's not like a voice telling me this, it's just my own thoughts, but they're so loud, so heavy. I just can't shake the feeling that I'm completely worthless as a dad, and that's why she's gone. I just keep chewing on it, Dr. Smith, over and over, trying to figure out exactly where I broke it all, and it just drags me down further into the mud.
